reviews.snippet:
The doctors are knowledgeable, experienced, polite, and supportive. They explain the patient's condition clearly and treat patients with respect, which is the biggest positive aspect of this hospital.

However, the nursing staff and security guards were often rude, unprofessional, and not patient-friendly. The general ward was not well maintained and lacked proper hygiene. There was a lot of mismanagement, and patients or their attendants were frequently sent from one counter to another and between different floors without proper guidance, making the process unnecessarily stressful.

Even the medicine department was poorly coordinated, resulting in long waits and confusion.

I also felt there was a noticeable difference in how patients were treated. Those using Ayushman Bharat or belonging to economically weaker sections appeared to receive less attention and and like they treat so rudely to all special to weak. Every patient deserves equal care, dignity, and professionalism, regardless of their financial background.

The hospital has capable doctors, but it urgently needs to improve its nursing services, hygiene, administration, and overall patient experience.

reviews.snippet:
⭐ 0/5 Rating – My Experience with Aurobindo Hospital, CHL, and Dr. Himendra Misra

My father was suffering from oral cancer, and he was under the treatment of Dr. Himendra Misra. During chemotherapy, my father repeatedly complained of severe headaches. We informed Dr. Misra several times, but we were told that the headaches were caused by oral cancer. No further investigation was suggested at that time.

After around five chemotherapy cycles, we were informed that we should decide within the next week whether to proceed with immunotherapy. This timeline was given by the doctor himself.

My father underwent regular blood tests throughout his treatment. However, after about 5½ chemotherapy cycles, he suddenly developed paralysis on one side of his body. We immediately took him back to the hospital. The doctor examined him and checked his blood sugar, which was around 105 mg/dL. Despite this being a normal reading, we were told that his sugar was "very low" and he was given IV fluids. We were then told to take him home because his condition was supposedly due to weakness from chemotherapy, even though his condition had not improved.

The very next day, his condition became much worse, so we returned to the hospital. This time we were told that the cancer had spread to his brain. We were also told, "We had already advised you to start immunotherapy, but you did not do it." This was extremely upsetting because the doctor himself had given us one week's time to make that decision.

We were then advised to get an MRI of the brain and were referred to Aurobindo Hospital under the Ayushman scheme. After spending almost the entire day completing admission formalities, my father finally underwent an MRI during the night. Later, we were informed by the neurosurgery team that brain surgery was required.

At that stage, my father's condition was already extremely poor because of chemotherapy, and we believed he was not fit for such a major operation. We requested medical management instead, but we felt pressured toward surgery. When we expressed our concerns, we were repeatedly told to take him home and look after him.

For the next 8–9 days, different doctors repeatedly suggested shifting him to the palliative care ward. We were also told that no further treatment would be provided and that only oxygen support could be given, which could also be managed at home. My father was unconscious, yet we were never given a clear explanation for his unconsciousness. His brain clot and neurological condition appeared to be managed mainly by the oncology team, even though neurologists were available. We were repeatedly told that nothing more could be be done.

Eventually, we discharged my father while he was still unconscious. The discharge summary stated that we were leaving against medical advice, even though we had repeatedly been told by the doctors to take him home. Shortly after bringing him home, my father passed away.

This entire experience was deeply painful for our family. We felt there was poor communication, inadequate explanations, lack of empathy, and a lack of coordinated care. The assistants were unprofessional, and many doctors did not communicate with us respectfully or clearly.

Based on my family's experience, I give 0/5 stars to Aurobindo Hospital, CHL Hospital, and Dr. Himendra Misra.
